resolution_matrix.empty_resolution_rule: Empty Posture carries no bonus and no damage of its own. For resolution, the enemy chooses which empty-type to treat it as (rule 6): an enemy with Attack treats EP as Posture (Attack beats Posture → EP takes 1); an enemy with Posture treats EP as Empty Move (Posture beats Move → EP takes 1). Enemies playing Move or Block pick the empty-type that neutralises the match, so Move-vs-EP and Block-vs-EP resolve as neutral. Empty Move resolves symmetrically: Block treats it as Move (Move loses to Block → EM takes 1).

edges.note: defender A also takes -1 damage dealt
enemy with Attack treats EP as Posture → attack still hits, EP takes 1
enemy with Posture treats EP as Empty Move → posture beats move, EP takes 1
mirror of A-vs-EP: EP actor takes 1 damage
mirror of P-vs-EP: EP actor takes 1 damage
enemy with Block treats EM as Move → block beats move, EM takes 1
mirror of B-vs-EM: EM actor takes 1 damage

resolution_matrix.empty_posture_vs_attack: ep takes -1 damage; attack still hits (now encoded as edge A→EP)
resolution_matrix.empty_move_vs_block: em takes -1 damage; block still hits (now encoded as edge B→EM)

data.notes: How the players upgrade the game: any VersionedEntry (rule, effect, skill, class, creature, item, protocol parameter) can receive a proposal version on a Radicle branch; signed votes accumulate weight; a deterministic rebalance script measures the proposal and counter-proposes linked deltas within a tolerance; on success the branch merges to develop and clients load the new canonical version at their next session. Parameters here are themselves VersionedEntries so the governance can govern itself.

versions.notes: Supersedes the prose in schema.json sync_contract.radicle_branch_layout; schema.json now points here.

main.writes: merge from develop by the release script only

develop.content: accepted proposals waiting for the next release
develop.writes: merge from proposals/* by the tally script when governance_voting thresholds pass

proposals/<entry_id>-<unix_ts>.content: one new version object appended to exactly one entry (or one linked set produced by the rebalance script)
proposals/<entry_id>-<unix_ts>.writes: proposer + rebalance script counter-proposals + vote_log appends

forks/<fork_name>.content: a group's larger rule-set divergence (own data/ tree)
forks/<fork_name>.writes: fork owners; may open a proposals/* branch to merge back wholesale

release.step: tag data/ on main as data-vX.Y.Z; clients compare rules_snapshot_commit at session open and prompt to update; a running Dimension keeps its snapshot until it is closed or its owners vote to migrate

file_rules: never edit a version object in place; append a new version with parent_version set
ids are never reused; a removed entry becomes status rejected with weight 0
proposals touch one entry unless produced by the rebalance script, which may touch the rebalance_links closure

versions.notes: Weight is the consensus confidence in a version, in [0,1]. The engine loads the highest-weight non-rejected version of each entry at session start.

data.who_may_vote: any peer with a signing key; weight of a vote scales with proven use of the entry (usage_evidence in evt_vote) so people who actually play with an effect/class decide its fate
data.vote_weight_formula: w = base(0.01) * (1 + log2(1 + times_used_in_dimension)) * (1 + 0.1 * dimensions_played_in); capped at 0.10 per peer per proposal

proposal_lifecycle.enter: branch created with new version object at weight 0.0

proposal_lifecycle.during: vote_log appends; weight = clamp(sum(+1 w) - sum(-1 w), 0, 1); rebalance script may append counter-proposal versions

proposal_lifecycle.enter: at tally time weight >= accept_threshold AND distinct voters >= quorum AND age >= min_age_s AND rebalance_within_tolerance
at tally time weight <= reject_threshold OR age > max_age_s without reaching quorum
automatically for the previous canonical version when a new one becomes canonical; its weight is set to the new version's weight minus 0.01 so it remains the fallback

data.in_dimension_voting: votes cast inside an owned Dimension apply immediately to that Dimension's local snapshot if its owners agree (local override), and are forwarded as evt_vote to the global proposal; the rebalance script may counter-propose and the local override is replaced if the owners accept within tolerance
data.vote_integrity: each vote is a signed hashgraph event; the tally script rejects duplicates per (peer_id, entry_id, version) and votes whose usage_evidence is not backed by TurnCommit history

versions.notes: The author's intent: no class, skill or effect becomes too strong; a buff to one thing is paid for by respective changes elsewhere, or a nerf comes with a compensating property. The script is deterministic so every peer can re-run it and verify the counter-proposal.

power_score.effect: expected_damage_per_action(rule_21 formula over the 12 characters' stat spreads) + 0.5*num_effect_types + 0.25*permanent_bonus + 0.5*channeling + 1.0*every_bonus(∀) - 0.3*element_cost_count

tolerance.explanation: a proposal passes if its power_score stays within 15% of the pre-proposal score OR the linked counter-deltas bring the mean of the rebalance_links closure back within 5%

counter_proposal_algorithm: else walk rebalance_links (breadth-first, depth <= 2) and distribute -delta proportionally to each linked entry's current power_score, producing a new version per linked entry with origin rebalance_script and parent_version = their canonical

if the proposal is a nerf (delta < 0) prefer adding a compensating property on the same entry (e.g. extra every_bonus, lower element_cost) over touching linked entries, when such a property keeps |delta| within tolerance
attach the counter-proposals to the same proposals/* branch; the original proposer may accept (vote +1 on the set) or amend
data.run_at: every tally_interval_s and on every new proposal push
data.transparency: the script writes rebalance_report.json next to the proposal with before/after power_score for every touched entry

versions.notes: Original paper text. Two separate Rule 0 paragraphs existed (tileset rule, character deck rule); Rule 25 was a third, later setup paragraph. Superseded by v1.1.0 which merges all three.

data.text:
Rule 0 (Initial setup tileset rule): The standard 3x4 tileset from the deck of the effects, depose two cards face down in each field. Depose on each tile one creature or one skill card at random. Randomly depose two class cards over the tiles occupied by monsters.

Rule 0 (Initial setup character deck rule): For each player
- Draw two character cards, choose one and discard the other (Your character card enters the tileset).
- Deal 10 effect cards and 4 skill cards: You may put any of them in your deck and the rest in your archives.
- Deal 2 class cards: discard one and put the other one initially on board over your face up archive column.
- Draw as many Attack, Block / Move / Posture cards as you want to create a deck of minimum 15 cards.

versions.notes: Folded Rule 25 into Phase A of this rule on 2026-10-19 per author decision; Rule 25 is now superseded. Author-written text used verbatim.

data.text:
Rule 0 (Initial setup: tileset rule and character deck rule).

Tileset. Over a tile-set 3x4 (4x4 or 5x5, depending on the count of the players):
- First distribute two effects on each tile as traps.
- Then shuffle the monsters and skills cards in one pile and distribute at random one more card of them over each tile.
- Finally each player may choose its starting entry point in order determined by the Will stat. Every next player cannot choose a location that is nearby any other non-ally player. Remember that you cannot choose an entry point that has a monster (green) card deposed already, and you still have to resolve the entry point traps.
Then you choose on which trap to depose your character clockwise, starting with the character with the highest Will (the character is counted as a Move action, and you may play Instants during this action). The player puts his character on a tile at least two tiles away from the enemy. If you put your character on a monster-occupied tile, you are in immediate combat with it: apply the effects as traps and put them face up on that tile simulating the monster's hand.

Character deck.
- Draw two character cards, choose one and discard the other (your character card enters the tileset).
- Deal 10 effect cards and 4 skill cards: you may put any of them in your deck and the rest in your archives.
- Deal 2 class cards: discard one and put the other one initially on board over your face-up archive column.
- Draw as many Attack / Block / Move / Posture cards as you want to create a deck of minimum 15 cards.

Each character has three actions (turns) per round chosen from Attack, Block, Move, Posture. Monsters have their own action count written on the card; monsters with four actions per round force the player to replace one action with Empty Posture. A player may decide which round to enter the Dimension tileset; permanents may be cast outside the dimension so their effects are ready on the entry tile.

Once a tile is Attacked or Moved towards, it turns face up and becomes 'open'. If there is a creature there, it awakens. If there are only effects there, the tile is a trap set with 20 power for each element used in the effects. All effects on the tile activate once as traps.

An awakened creature defends its tile and never leaves it. It attacks any character in contact. If there is an awakened creature on a tile, all effects there go into that defender's hand. All defenders use D6 randomized actions. Monsters regenerate if no enemy is in contact with them. The next enemy player controls the monster (the player after the one currently in contact).

To disable a trap, at some point all the effects on it must fail to kill you (you survive the damage) or fail to lock you (because of high stats). It is enough for one element of an effect not to work for the whole effect to fail. If a trap or monster kills or locks your character, you lose one time and may re-enter the Dimension once again fighting for a draw (Remi). All traps are resolved in one round.

Each monster in contact with a character typically throws 4 D6 to determine its current action: green=Block, blue/white=Move, red=Attack, black=Posture. Some monsters have custom patterns (BAAPM, AAAM) and throw those D6 combinations each action. When the Posture score is highest, the monster may choose the proper effect from its hand and skips throwing dice until all the effect's elements are emitted.

If the hero cannot or does not want to act, they play an empty action called Empty Posture. Empty Posture does not grant Posture's benefits (does not beat Move). Effects may still be made during Empty Posture. The Empty Posture card may alternatively be played as Empty Move (declared first). For combat calculations, the enemy chooses which empty-type to treat it as (Posture enemy picks Empty Move; Attack enemy picks Empty Posture). The Empty Posture card always returns to the hand after action evaluation.

Characters act simultaneously each turn (cards face-down). Sequence: (1) all characters/creatures in contact put their cards face down each turn; (2) cards flip face up and actions resolve — instants and skills may still be played before resolution; target is pointed out and damage is attempted. Characters/creatures in contact may play effects on their Posture or Empty Posture actions. After the final turn of a round, characters may discard remaining cards and draw up to five. Monsters do not discard. If an opponent has more actions per round than you, you may be forced to play Empty Posture (it cannot be converted to Empty Move when forced).

Each action within the round the player declares in order: (1) Empty Move (special way of playing Empty Posture — move halfway toward target, declared first); (2) turn up an action card (A/B/M/P/EP); (3) play Effects — effect declaration binds the current action to emit a specific element (first as ordered in effect description). There is NO stack — all skills and effects apply; if some effect/skill prohibits an action or emission it is applied finally as a replacement; (4) play skills / instants / class-card per-round abilities, OR point-buy an element/color to try to destroy a token.

You enter the dimension with your class card as a permanent. It is always cast with tokens of value 6 for each color. Some classes trigger once per round; some have a static always-on ability; some have a rechargeable ability that requires tapping the class card. To untap, emit each color of the class (count of elements of the same color is irrelevant). Untapping can span different rounds.

Each round the hero draws cards until their hand reaches 5. Used cards go to the character's deck discard pile. If deck is empty, reshuffle the discard pile into deck. A player may choose not to reshuffle.

A character may leave used cards in the archive instead of discarding (for deck refinement). Defeated monsters also go to the deck archive and may be used by effects like necromancy, summoning (substituting for a random library creature), possess, link — as outer-dimension allies. When the ally monster enters this dimension, it enters on your tile, moves with you, and acts as a player-managed monster for decision-making. You may always move an archived card to the discard pile.

Played cards go to the discard pile. A permanent-type card goes in front of the deck until destroyed; you must point-buy (roll dice summing ≤ your stat; place the highest die as a defense token with that color; you may repeat the roll if unhappy). Place over the permanent a small neutral die with value equal to the lowest color value. Tile token = big colored die placed to the right side of the tile (character card is a rectangle), set by point-buy, adds as a bonus to each creature on the tile. Permanent token = colored die positioned over a specific stat on the character card, applied as stat bonus. Stat penalty token = wooden die, same rule but placed below the stat number and subtracted.

Each turn (from the round) you oppose your actions, effects and skills to evaluate benefits and damage. Effect evaluation happens after emitting or point-buying all the effect's elements. Combo evaluation happens when all actions of it are performed. For each turn/action the sum is rounded at mathematical principle (round-half-up at the nearest multiple of 10) and applied as damage — see Rule 21.

versions.notes: Unified from the three prior Rule 14 entries (acquisition/trade, life, adjacency) on 2026-10-19 per author decision.

data.text:
Rule 14 covers three closely-related mechanics.

Part A — Acquisition / trade. Acquiring effects/skills happens via conquering a field with an effect, or obtaining one from a defeated character's deck. Place the acquired card in discard or archive pile. You may spend an action to trade archives with an adjacent character if one of you moves towards the other. With an adjacent hero you may also discard your cards into their discard pile, or place a just-played card in their discard pile instead of your own.

Part B — Life. Life of each creature/character = Σ Stats ÷ 10, rounded at mathematical principle (see Rule 21). All characters have Σ Stats = 40 → 4 life tokens. Monsters have varying Σ Stats (e.g. Dragon = 80 → 8 life tokens). Damage by effect is rounded at the same principle when the effect is cast. The total life token is a small neutral die, recalculated whenever damage is done or a new token of any kind of value ≥ 5 is added/updated over the tile or character.

Part C — Adjacency. Characters can be attacked only by another character or creature in the 8 surrounding tiles (horizontal, vertical, diagonal).

With every action the hero can target a field (Move) and/or an enemy (Attack/Move). Block does not target; it deals 1 damage to each enemy who attacked you. Empty Posture cannot perform targeting with effect or skill. If two characters target the same tile for a Move: only the one actually using Move moves there; on mirrored actions no one moves. Using Attack, you MAY follow (optional) the targeted hero if they move, as if performing a Move targeting the enemy's tile. You may also stay on your tile if you target the enemy/tile with Attack/Move (e.g. channeling an effect via point-buy).

Each character has a special combo (sequence of trained actions in a specific order). If you complete your combo and have contact with an enemy, you deal +1 bonus damage. Damage applies only while in contact. Combos are announced on full execution. Combo structure: 1st → 2nd → 3rd → {4th}. Combos are on the character card. 'Adept' means the character uses a specific element with power 20. Characters have an a-priori combo but may find other combo cards during play.

Skills may be played as instants (trick, bluff, intimidation, tripping, …) when a specified action is played, and may change the outcome. Multiple skills may be used over one action. Carefully pick the number of skills in the deck to avoid holding 5 skills with no action to play.

Each effect comprises one or more elements. The caster emits each element with power equal to their Stat for that element. Enemy resists with their Stat. (Except point-buy effects, which cannot be resisted.) If any element's power ≤ enemy's stat power, the effect is not successful (enemy saves) or deals zero on that element.

To cast, elements are emitted via contiguous Postures — one Posture emits one element in order. If the sequence is interrupted the cast fails. After casting, the effect goes to discard unless it is a Channeled or Permanent effect. Channeling may continue as long as the character stays on the same tile (uses environment to channel). Casting a permanent effect places it in front of the deck. Instant effects are the exception (see Rule 20). Postures must be contiguous — a two-element effect cannot be cast with Posture → Block → Posture.

Effect types: Point-buy — damage done via point-buy rather than stat-emit comparison. Damage — summarized damage by stat comparison per element spent. Instant — castable with any action, not only Posture. Shield token — add point-buy as colorless die (rounded up) in the emitted color over the tile; acts as tile-based extra life, cumulative. Non-Damage / Instant effects — put a value-1 die in the emitted element color over the castable card until cast or the condition expires. Point-buy mechanic — roll dice summing ≤ stat, keep highest. Apply as defense token / stat penalty by color on permanent/character/tile, OR as damage if the effect is Damage type. If sum exceeds stat (fail), you can repeat next action as a contiguous action (slower casting). Channeling — continuously cast the same effect next turn(s), even next round, as temporary permanent with point-buy defense tokens. Goes to discard when you stop channeling or when the last defense token is destroyed. Stat buy — effects summarize points spent to emit elements until some total is reached across multiple rounds.

versions.notes: 'Rounded up at mathematical principle' = round-half-up at the nearest multiple of 10 (0.5→1, 0.4→0). Not ceiling.

data.text: If the effect does Damage, the difference in Stats (yours − enemy's) per element equals the stat damage. The effect's Stat Damage is divided by 10 and rounded at mathematical principle (round-half-up), calculated each turn for completed effects when the defender has no tokens to destroy (defender chooses which token is destroyed). Example 1: fire delta 3 + water delta 2 = 5 points → rounded up to 10 → 1 damage. Example 2: instant effect does 2 points, then 2 more next action = 4 points → rounded down to 0 → 0 stat damage.
data.formula: damage = round_half_up(sum_of_stat_deltas / 10)   // 0.5 rounds up, 0.4 rounds down

data.text: Different effects can be cast simultaneously as long as they require the same elements. If two effects share a common element, the character casts in three steps: emit the first uncommon element + announce effect 1 → emit the shared element + announce effect 2 (effect 1 succeeds) → emit the second uncommon element (effect 2 succeeds). You may superimpose multiple effects with shared elements simultaneously, or chain them.
Two effects with the same name may be cast together using multicast. In some doubled effects a special rule marked with the ∀ ('every') symbol applies — 'every' here means at least two.

Any permanent effect can be destroyed by point-buying one of its elements with a die ≥ the token's value. Any token can be destroyed by point-buy. You cannot target more than one permanent/token at once (unless you have an Aura permanent). You choose EITHER to emit an element OR target one permanent/token, but not both (unless you have Aura). Only the class card requires destroying all its colors (ignoring count-per-color) against value 6.

data.description: Versioned, voteable data-layer schema for the Dimensions RPG (chaosD6). Every entity (rule, effect, skill, class, character, creature, item, etc.) is a VersionedEntry. Governance = Radicle git branches propose new versions, peers sign votes, a rebalance pass updates weights, and the engine loads the highest-weight canonical version at session start.

entry_contract.id: stable kebab-case id, unique across the collection; never reused
entry_contract.collection: which top-level file this entry lives in (see index.json collections)
entry_contract.name: human-readable name
tags: optional free-form tags used by the rebalance script to find related entries

versions.version: semver-ish string; v1.0.0 is the paper-rules original
versions.weight: float in [0.0, 1.0] — current consensus confidence; the engine picks the highest-weight non-rejected version at session start
versions.status: canonical | proposal | superseded | rejected | resolved (contradictions only)
versions.origin: paper_rules | player_vote | rebalance_script | fork_merge | playtest_patch | runtime_contract
versions.author_peer_id: Radicle peer id of the proposer; empty for paper_rules
versions.parent_version: the version this one derives from, or null if root
rebalance_links: list of entity ids that are mechanically coupled; if the rebalance script bumps this entry it will propose counter-balance deltas on these

vote_log.weight_contribution: float; signed to add/subtract from weight

versions.notes: optional free-form rationale from the proposer
versions.data: the actual mechanical payload; shape depends on the collection

collection_shapes.effects: data = { element_cost:[element_id], effect_types:[damage|instant|point_buy|permanent|channeling|stat_buy|shield_token], text, dispelable_by:[entry_id], every_bonus (for ∀ doubled casts) }
collection_shapes.classes: data = { colors:[element_id], ability_kind: once_per_round|static|tap, text, destroy_cost:'point-buy each color at value 6' }
collection_shapes.actions: data = { code:A|B|M|P|EP|EM, text, rps_wins_against:[action_code], rps_loses_against:[action_code], can_cast_non_instant_effects:bool }
collection_shapes.characters: data = { combo:[action_code], adept_element, stats:{vitality, world, matter, will}, life:int, actions_per_round:int }
collection_shapes.creatures: data = { stats:{...}, life:int, actions_per_round:int, dice_pattern:'BAAPM|AAAM|BMAP', innate_effect:effect_id, on_action_rider:{action_code, bonus_damage} }
collection_shapes.game_modes: data = { tileset_size, player_count, win_condition, time_per_turn_s, special_rules_text }
collection_shapes.contradictions: data = { source_entries:[entry_id], description, evidence:[...], proposed_resolutions:[{resolution_id, text}], chosen_resolution? }
collection_shapes.sync_protocol: data = free-form protocol parameters per entry (tiers, phases, intervals, flows, algorithms); numbers are the tunables the community votes on
collection_shapes.hashgraph_events: data = { scope: dimension|door|strong_region, emitted_by, finality, payload:{field: type-description} }
collection_shapes.dimension_session: data = { shape: {field: type-description} } describing dimension.json / doors/<DoorId>.json / local client state
collection_shapes.governance: data = free-form per entry: branch layout, voting thresholds, rebalance script contract, fork policy, write permissions

sync_contract.description: How the data layer participates in the P2P / Radicle / hashgraph sync model.
sync_contract.write_boundary: The engine NEVER mutates versions in place. All changes land as a new version appended to `versions`. The highest-weight non-rejected version is the active one at a given turn.
sync_contract.merge_strategy: git merge is additive on the `versions` array; conflicting metadata on the same version (same id+version) picks the higher weight.
sync_contract.rebalance_cycle: A deterministic script walks `rebalance_links`; a buff above tolerance proposes equal-magnitude counters on linked entries; proposals go to proposals/<entry_id>-<ts>.
sync_contract.votes_in_dimension_vs_global: A player's vote weight on an entry is scaled by their time-of-use with that entry inside their owned Dimension; measured from session telemetry.

data.notes: Skills are played as instants attached to a matching action card. Point-buy skills roll against the listed stat.

data.text: On successful attack: +1 damage; cannot perform any other action except Attack until end of round.
Swap places with the enemy (walk over them and go behind). Negate enemy's Move. Alt: the enemy or ally is moved one tile away; step over them.
Negate enemy's Posture or Empty Posture (enemy may replace with another action; Empty Move is still possible). While sharing a tile, neither may use Posture or Empty Posture.
Permanent. On your Attack action, enemy's Block action does not cause you combat damage. Your Attack action does not trigger traps and the follow rule is not applied.
Nearby enemies cannot Attack anything besides you. Nearby enemies cannot use Block against you.
Subtract the Shield permanent die value from effect damage before rounding. Destroy this permanent if effect damage is taken.
Nearby enemies cannot use Attack against you.
Permanent until doing action. You, any permanent, and any token you control (besides Sanctuary) are invincible until you emit or perform any action.
The enemy cannot use Posture; any Empty Posture is always played as Empty Move (enemy cannot emit non-instant effects).
−1 combat damage (one less damage done to you this action).
Negate enemy's action and replace it with Empty Posture.
The enemy cannot use Attack until end of round.
You may use another action this turn; choose both or one for the calculations.
Counter target non-permanent skill; emit an element against the enemy, subtract the element stat from the enemy's stat.

data.notes: Machine-readable contract for the peer-to-peer Dimension sync model: hashgraph-style gossip between players who share map regions, once-per-turn sync inside a Dimension, and a once-per-interval Radicle git push as the only (decentralized) central point. Every entry is a VersionedEntry so the protocol parameters themselves are voteable.

versions.notes: Derived from Rule 14 Part C (8-neighbour adjacency) and the author's region concept: players in strongly referenced regions share the same turn state and handshake every action; players that can reach each other within one real-time sync interval share the same map hashgraph to avoid collisions on first contact; far players sync once per turn or only at the Radicle push.

tiers.label: Contact region
tiers.membership: players/creatures whose tiles are adjacent or within strong_radius_tiles of each other, or that currently target each other (attack/move/follow)
tiers.consensus: every action is a signed hashgraph event; the action resolves only when all strong-region members have gossiped it (virtual voting, no leader)
tiers.failure_mode: a member that does not answer the handshake within handshake_timeout_s is treated as playing Empty Posture for that action (rule_6) and marked lagging

tiers.label: One-interval reach region
tiers.membership: players that could enter each other's strong region before the next Radicle push (max move distance x actions x rounds per radicle_push_interval_s)
tiers.consensus: members exchange a signed TurnCommit at the end of each turn so that the shared map hashgraph is identical before any first contact
tiers.failure_mode: missing commits are filled on first contact via hashgraph merge (see sync_divergence_merge)

tiers.label: Unmet / distant region
tiers.membership: everyone else inside the Dimension, including clans and new players that have never met
tiers.consensus: none in real time; the Radicle branch ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/ is the eventual rendezvous point
tiers.failure_mode: state is allowed to diverge; divergence is reconciled on first contact or at the next push

data.tier_promotion: a far/reachable peer is promoted to strong as soon as a position event places it inside strong_radius_tiles; promotion triggers a full state handshake (sync_join_flow step adopt_hashgraph_part)

versions.notes: Mirrors the paper's simultaneous action rule (Rule 7) and the declaration sequence (Rule 8). Commit/reveal keeps face-down cards secret until everyone in the strong region has committed.

phases.name: commit
phases.payload: hash(action_card + effects + skills + salt) per actor

phases.name: reveal
phases.payload: the plaintext declaration + salt; peers verify the hash

phases.name: instants
phases.payload: optional Skills/instants/class abilities/point-buy responses, same commit-reveal in a mini-round

phases.name: evaluate
phases.payload: each peer runs the deterministic resolver (battle_system_core) locally and signs the resulting state hash

phases.name: finalize
phases.payload: action event is final when the state hashes of all members match; mismatch -> dispute (see sync_divergence_merge)

data.dice: D6 rolls (Rule 5 monsters, point buy) are produced by combining every member's revealed salt: roll = 1 + (sha256(concat(salts) + roll_index) mod 6). No peer can bias the roll alone.
data.monster_control: The monster's actions are generated by the peer that currently controls it per Rule 3, but the dice come from the shared salt so the result is verifiable by all.
data.transport_for_now: plain JSON messages over the P2P channel (WebRTC data channel or Radicle node link); binary encoding is a later optimisation

message_envelope.type: string (one of the ids in hashgraph_events.json)
message_envelope.self_parent: hash of the actor's previous event
message_envelope.other_parent: hash of the most recent event received from another peer
message_envelope.signature: detached signature over the whole envelope minus signature

versions.notes: Players who do not share a strong region do not need every action; they need the turn boundary so turn counters stay aligned and the map hashgraph stays mergeable.

data.when: after the last action of a turn is finalized in the player's strong region (or after Empty Posture when alone)

payload.region_state_hash: hash of the strong region's finalized state
payload.map_delta: list of tile changes since previous TurnCommit (revealed tiles, token changes, owner changes, new permanents)
payload.hashgraph_head: hash of the latest finalized event

data.turn_counter_rule: a Dimension-wide turn is the max turn seen; peers that are behind receive the missing TurnCommits before acting (they cannot skip turns, see rule_6 for Empty Posture catch-up)
data.far_region_notification: when a TurnCommit or Radicle poll reveals previously unknown map items (new clans, new DoorIds, long-distance permanents) the client raises the disturbance_in_the_force UI event and applies the delta to unrevealed tiles only

entries.name: Interval Radicle push (the single decentralized rendezvous)

versions.notes: The author's design: one random active player holding a DoorId pushes the merged DoorId.json every interval. Everyone else polls git. This is the only centralization point and it is itself a decentralized Radicle repo.

paths.rules_snapshot: ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/rules_snapshot_commit (commit hash of data/ used by this session)

pusher_election.method: deterministic lottery among the active members of the DoorId's hashgraph: pusher = member with min( sha256(peer_id + hashgraph_head + interval_index) )
pusher_election.fallback: if the elected pusher does not push within pusher_grace_s, the next-lowest hash pushes; duplicate pushes are harmless because the merge is additive

data.commit_content: doors/<DoorId>.json = { magnet_id, turn, hashgraph_head, members, map_summary (revealed tiles count, owned towers/crystals/mines), last_push_at } - see dimension_session.json for the exact shape
data.merge_policy: git merge on the branch is additive: doors/ files from different clans never conflict (one file per DoorId); dimension.json conflicts resolve to the higher turn counter
data.git_poll_effect: on poll, if a new/changed doors/<DoorId>.json is seen that is not in the local hashgraph, the client schedules a background reconciliation and raises disturbance_in_the_force

entries.name: Joining a Dimension (open / follow a friend / new location)

versions.notes: The DoorId behaves like a magnet URI: it names a hashgraph head and the peers that hold it, not a server. Three ways in: open a new Dimension, join a friend/clan (adopt their hashgraph part), or appear at a brand-new location from an old push.

steps: generate DimensionName/Id and the initial tileset per rule_0_setup (size by expected player count)
create the local hashgraph genesis event with rules_snapshot_commit
publish ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/dimension.json + doors/<first DoorId>.json to Radicle (the opening players now own the Dimension)
optionally register the DoorId in the Firebase directory for discovery only
pick ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/doors/<DoorId> of the friend or clan
connect to the pe= peers of the magnet and request the hashgraph part they hold (adopt_hashgraph_part)
verify the chain from genesis to hashgraph_head against signatures and the rules snapshot
enter on a free tile inside the friend's reachable region per rule_0_setup entry-point constraints (not adjacent to a non-ally; traps still resolve)
become a holder of that DoorId; you may now be elected as its Radicle pusher
pick a DoorId whose last push is older than the current interval (state is known to be stale)

allocate a fresh map region: extend the tileset by one block (same size as the initial tileset, rule_0_setup) adjacent to the existing bounds and seed it with traps/monsters/skills/classes per rule_0_setup
mint a new DoorId for the new region with its own hashgraph branch rooted at the pushed head
push doors/<newDoorId>.json immediately so active players learn about it on their next poll
play on the stale snapshot; reconciliation with the live clan happens on first contact (sync_divergence_merge)

data.leave_dimension: a LeaveEvent is gossiped; the character card stays on its tile as a map item until the next Radicle push records the departure
data.firebase_role: discovery/coordination only: list of DimensionNames with their Radicle repo ids and last push time. Never game state.

entries.name: Reconciling divergent map parts on first contact

versions.notes: Two clans that never met hold two hashgraph parts that may disagree about tiles neither has actually touched. Merge rules keep the game fair without a server.

data.trigger: a TurnCommit or position event places two peers from different hashgraph parts inside each other's reachable region, or a Radicle poll shows a new DoorId
algorithm: exchange hashgraph heads and find the common ancestor (the Radicle push both parts descend from)
replay both event sets in consensus order (virtual voting timestamps: median of received-times across members)
tiles touched by only one part: take that part's state as-is

tiles touched by both parts: apply the deterministic resolver turn by turn in consensus order; tokens that cannot both exist (two owners of one tower) go to the earlier consensus timestamp, the later owner's cards return to their discard pile
hidden/unrevealed tiles: keep the seed from the Radicle genesis so both parts reveal identical traps/monsters (rule_2)
turn counters: the merged region adopts max(turn); the lagging part plays Empty Posture for the skipped actions (rule_6)
emit a MergeEvent signed by all strong-region members; the merged part becomes one DoorId holder set (old DoorIds remain as aliases)
data.dispute: if the resolver hashes differ at any step, the minority peers replay with the majority's events; a peer that still differs after max_retries is marked desynced and must rejoin via join_near_friend
data.cheat_resistance: only signed events in a validated chain are replayed; a peer cannot introduce cards it never drew because draws (rule_10) are events with shared-salt randomness

data.notes: Towers, Crystals, Mines, Buildings, Nexus, Doors, Libraries, Stashes, Trade Centers, and generic Walls/Rivers/Lava. Each entry carries requirements and yields in the data block.
Starting location; mind-control over guardians while standing on it
Entry point for intruders; hire other players for raid; accept raid offers once per day.

data.behavior: attacks only attacking creatures or gives bonus
